scene: Inferno XX — the diviners walking forward while their heads face behind
story: Dante and Virgil reach the fourth bolgia where diviners, astrologers and sorcerers advance slowly along the ditch.
Their heads are twisted backward upon their bodies; they must walk onward while looking behind themselves.
Tears fall from the eyes down their backs and across their bodies, a physical detail that makes Dante weep in sympathy.
Virgil rebukes Dante's pity in this scene and identifies figures including Amphiaraus, Tiresias, Aruns and Manto.
Virgil recounts the story of Manto and the founding of Mantua, distinguishing this account in the poem from other traditions.
The procession continues; the travelers turn onward toward the fifth bolgia, which belongs to the next stage.
